about: The cases laid out by hand that tools/test.mjs compares the solver with: two takes, each as the numbers of its layouts (the frame, where the sharp picture lies, the faces, the text), never as pictures: the tests draw a placeholder. picture: the source's box in the frame; window: what of it shows where it is clipped; a caption block: left, width, the distance of its bottom from the frame's bottom, its type and lines. winners: what the solver puts first for each case with the weights of tools/weights.json and the skill's own type sizes (card: the hook as a card across the top, which the hand laid out; hook: as the solver tries it first, a short text in the middle); basis says who stands behind it: hand (the layout made by hand on the still), judged (people compared stills), solver (nobody has looked: it only keeps a change of the weights from passing unseen).

p1.what: An upright phone take, 1080×1920: one person speaking to the phone from close by, the face large, the eyes at half the height, the chin at 77 % of it. Laid out by hand on one still on 2026-11-16.
p1.head: This box was read from the top of the head, not from the hairline (on the hand's still the hair's top lies 15 px above it, the receding hairline about 65 px of the source below it; the phone looks up at the face). The solver keeps a third of a box's height above it for the skull (defaults.mjs, free.above): for this box that would keep 300 px of wall clear that the hand used. Every run on this take keeps the margin it has as read, a fiftieth.

p2.what: A wide take, 1280×720: one person in the middle of a public interview, a still at second 45. The face read off a grid by hand (the eyes at y 200). Laid out by hand on 2026-11-17; people judged the sharpness on these stills: 1.5× crisp, 1.875× mildly soft but fine, 2.67× too soft to publish.
